record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: cmc disks constrained to a slab
record.original_question: Let C be a closed curve contained in a slab S_w ⊂ ℝ³ of width w, and let H ≠ 0 satisfy |H| < 2/w. Does there exist a topological disk of constant mean curvature H spanning C and entirely contained in the same slab S_w?

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.3. Let H
ot=0 and let C be a closed curve contained in a slab \mathcal{S}_w\subset\mathbb{R}^{3} of width w such that |H|<2/w. Does an H-topological disk exist spanning C and included in \mathcal{S}_w?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathcal{S}_w \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote a closed slab of width $w>0$, i.e., the region bounded by two parallel planes at distance $w$. Let $C \subset \mathcal{S}_w$ be a closed (Jordan) curve, and let $H \neq 0$ be a real number satisfying $|H| < 2/w$. Does there exist an immersed topological disk $\Sigma$ of constant mean curvature $H$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that $\partial \Sigma = C$ and $\Sigma \subset \mathcal{S}_w$?
artifact.category_tag: Constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey of open problems on compact CMC surfaces with boundary. Web search returned no published resolution; classical existence results (e.g., Hildebrandt) give CMC disks spanning curves in balls under |H|≤1/R, but no analogous slab-confined existence result confirming or refuting the |H|<2/w threshold appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Stable constant mean curvature surfaces with free boundary in slabs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies stable CMC surfaces with free boundary in slabs but does not address the spanning disk existence question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on CMC surfaces in slabs does not resolve the spanning-disk existence question.

status_evidence.title: Constant Mean Curvature Disks with Circular Boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a (possibly branched) CMC disk spanning C is known when C lies in a ball of radius R with |H|≤1/R; the slab analogue is not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Classical existence results are for balls, not slabs.
